title: Penn State lacks ‘a mental toughness’ it takes to reach the next level as a team
author: Andrew Deal | Wrestling Editor
description:
Throughout the offseason and in the beginning of the season, Matt Campbell consistently talked about how Penn State responds to adversity will really show the type of team he has in his first year.

The Nittany Lions have faced plenty of adversity since, and their response has been inconsistent. Penn State is sitting at 6-5, coming off one of the worst losses in program history, and had multiple opportunities to put away the game against Rutgers on Saturday.

It’s the team’s mental toughness that Campbell said Tuesday is something leading to losses like the one against the Scarlet Knights.

“I think we lack a mental toughness that it takes to be the best version of us for 60 minutes,” Campbell said. “I've been saying it to be quite honest with you. I said it in fall camp before we started the season, and there is a mental maturity and a toughness that it takes to be your best.”

The Nittany Lions have struggled to finish out games, which has allowed teams to stay in contests, a few of which have ultimately won.

This is due in part to the lack of mental toughness Penn State has. It didn’t develop in the offseason and hasn’t developed during the season despite multiple opportunities to battle through adversity.

“The reality of it, those are areas that we have to grow,” Campbell said. “And the head coach is the mental toughness coach, and so it's a direct reflection on I think where our gaps are and where we have to continue to strain to do a great job.”

There’s not a specific group or area where Penn State has lacked the mental toughness. Sometimes it’s been the offense that’s struggled to carry momentum from the first half to the second half. Other times it’s the defense.

On certain occasions it’s both, which helped Rutgers and Wisconsin come back and win.

On Saturday, it was the defense that faltered at the end of the game, allowing a miraculous touchdown score as time was expiring.

“You can't relax,” D’Anton Lynn said. “There's always things you can do better. And I think that everyone thought that he was going to get tackled, and I think that there was just a little bit of relax. And you have to pursue to the ball relentlessly.”

Lynn mentioned there’s been times when the defense has been tired. But the exhaustion is physical — not mental — which is something he said has to be strong when his players get tired.

“At the end of the day, when you're tired and gassed, you still have to do the little things right, and that's something that we have not been able to do for four straight quarters,” Lynn said.

Both Lynn and Campbell keyed in on the defense's struggle to get off the field. On Saturday, Penn State limited Rutgers to a 4-of-16 mark on third downs.

The 25% conversion rate on third downs took a big jump on fourth downs, despite the smaller sample size. The Scarlet Knights converted on 3-of-4 fourth down opportunities to extend offensive drives.

“It doesn't matter if you play 80 plays, if you play 100 plays,” Lynn said. “If you're out there for a 5-yard drive or a 20-yard drive. We have a job to get off the field, and regardless of the circumstances, we're not doing that enough at the end of games.”

Penn State has shown the ability to be mentally tough this season. After a four-game losing streak to begin Big Ten play, it could’ve just thrown the season away, but it didn’t, responding with three straight wins.

Rocco Becht knows that the team, which has brought pieces from all around the country, should get out of the tough times quicker this time around than the first time with the losing streak. He said that mental toughness is something “you got to be able to go out and find it and be able to take it to the next level.”

While the team has battled through adversity already this season, it’s still not where it needs to be at the end of the season, when a team at this level should be playing at its best.

“I feel like that's an area for us that is a gap that we're growing in with great consistency,” Campbell said. “We're just not as consistent as we need to be to be the team we want to become.”

title: Penn State women’s volleyball ends winning streak, Big Ten Tournament run with semifinal loss to Wisconsin
author: Noah Radio | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State women’s volleyball’s first-ever Big Ten Tournament run is over. The Nittany Lions ended their win streak, falling to Wisconsin in the semifinals Tuesday night, 3-1.

Stars shined on both sides of the court. For Penn State, Big Ten Player of the Year Kennedy Martin led all scorers with 27 kills. For Wisconsin, the Big Ten Freshman of the Year, Decelise Champion, came up with a championship performance. The 17-year-old recorded 23 kills while battling cramps throughout the match.

Penn State won the first point of the match with a big swing by Martin. The senior racked up 28 kills, three aces and 12 digs when Penn State beat the Badgers in Madison on Nov. 8.

Wisconsin bounced back quickly, taking its first lead at 5-4 thanks to a kill by Champion.

The two sides battled hard through the opening stages, and neither team led by more than three points before the first media timeout. Penn State went into the break up 15-13 after a service ace by Ava Falduto.

The Badgers flew out with a 5-2 run, and Katie Schumacher-Cawley called a timeout trailing 18-17. Penn State tied it up with a powerful kill by Whitney Lauenstein, but Wisconsin’s front line kept firing.

Jaela Auguste powered the Badgers to a 24-21 lead and an opportunity to win the first set. Penn State staved off defeat for one point, but then Champion swung the Badgers to a 1-0 match lead. The victory continued a five-match streak at the Big Ten Tournament of the lower seed winning the first set.

The second set was more of the same. Martin scored three of Penn State’s first four points and then collided with Falduto, the libero, as the Nittany Lions went up 5-3. The much smaller Falduto took the brunt of the contact, but stayed in the game.

Penn State opened up its largest lead of either set, 10-6, and then flew into the media timeout up 15-9.

The teams split the next four points, and Wisconsin coach Kelly Sheffield called his first timeout down 17-11. Martin already reached 10 kills, and she added another moments later to extend the lead to 20-13.

Back-to-back Wisconsin service errors and four Emmi Sellman kills helped Penn State reach set point with a 24-17 lead and ultimately take set two, 25-17.

In the third set, Wisconsin jumped out to a quick 3-0 lead. Penn State inched back to a 4-3 deficit, but the 6-foot-6 Champion worked Wisconsin’s lead up to 8-5. From there, the top-10 squads went blow for blow, much like the first set.

Auguste, the junior middle blocker, won Wisconsin’s 15th point of the set with her 12th kill of the match. After the media timeout, Penn State reeled off three straight points to retake the lead.

However, the Badgers countered with a 5-1 scoring run to take a 20-17 lead, and Schumacher-Cawley called a timeout.

Penn State crawled the score up to 23-23 with a rare kill by the star setter Alexis Stucky, but the redshirt senior couldn’t convert from the service line, and Wisconsin took a 24-23 lead.

With a huge swing by Champion, the Badgers took the third set. It was the freshman’s 15th kill of the match and sixth of the set.

Early in the fourth, Wisconsin jumped out to a 6-3 lead, but a kill and an ace by Martin and a kill by Kendall Northern tied it up at six.

The sides split the next six points, and when Penn State tied things up at nine, it was Stucky who dumped it right in front of Auguste. Stucky got in Auguste’s face at the net after the point, but it was all friendly competition. The pair, along with Martin, played together at Florida in 2024, and Stucky told the referee between points, “That’s my best friend.”

Things stayed tight through the media timeout. Wisconsin slightly broke ahead, as Lynney Tarnow picked up her ninth kill of the match to take a 15-14 lead before the break.

The Badgers slowly but surely crept towards match point. Martin came up with a trio of kills, but two service errors squandered opportunities.

Wisconsin reached match point with a five-point lead, but Penn State worked the score to 24-23 before ultimately succumbing to another Auguste kill.

Up Next

Wisconsin now moves on to face No. 1 Nebraska in the Big Ten championship game at 8 p.m. on Wednesday, while Penn State awaits its seeding fate in the NCAA Tournament with the selection show airing at 6 p.m. Sunday.

title: Texas trip, island bowl predicted by national outlets in Week 13 bowl projections
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Week 12 is in the books, and Penn State’s bowl projections have taken a turn after a disastrous loss to Rutgers on Saturday.

Various national outlets have the Nittany Lions traveling across the country, or even leaving the mainland, for the postseason contest.

Here’s what bowls national outlets project for the Nittany Lions.

ESPN: Armed Forces Bowl

Mark Schlabach of ESPN projects Penn State to face Army at Amon G. Carter Stadium, the home of TCU, in Fort Worth, Texas. The game will take place at 4:30 p.m. CT on Wednesday, Dec. 23.

It would mark the first time a team from the Big Ten participated in the bowl, as well as the 15th instance of a military academy playing. So far, 14 of the last 20 contests have featured either Army, Navy or Air Force.

The Black Knights are 4-0 in the Armed Forces Bowl with wins over SMU in 2010, San Diego State in 2017, Houston in 2018 and Missouri in 2021. Army’s 70 points scored against Houston were the most by a single team in the game’s history by far.

Army is amidst a three-game losing streak coming at the hands of Memphis, Air Force and East Carolina. The Black Knights must beat either Rice or Navy to gain bowl eligibility.

CBS, ESPN: Duke’s Mayo Bowl

CBS Sports and Kyle Bonagura of ESPN have Penn State traveling to Charlotte, North Carolina, for the Duke’s Mayo Bowl at Bank of America Stadium at 3:30 p.m. ET on Dec. 26.

CBS has the Nittany Lions facing North Carolina, while Bonagura has them facing Clemson in the postseason for the second straight year.

The Tar Heels have improved from its 4-8 record last season, currently 5-6 with only an in-state game against NC State left to play. Meanwhile, the Tigers have a 7-4 record with their game on Saturday against No. 21 South Carolina at home.

The Nittany Lions have only played the Tar Heels once in 1943, with North Carolina coming out on top with a 19-0 victory in Chapel Hill.

Penn State faced Clemson for the second time in last season’s Pinstripe Bowl, the first meeting between the programs since 1987. While the Tigers took the earlier game, the Nittany Lions tied the series with a 22-10 victory at Yankee Stadium on Dec. 27, 2025.

On3: Cactus Bowl

On3 has Penn State going out west to Sun Devil Stadium in Tempe, Arizona, to face UCF in the Cactus Bowl at 4:30 p.m. MST on Dec. 26. It would be the first time the Nittany Lions play in the bowl.

The Knights mirror the Nittany Lions’ 6-5 record after beating Iowa State, 48-17, on Saturday. UCF upset then-No. 2 BYU in double overtime on Oct. 24, the highlight of its season.

Penn State and UCF have played four times between 2002 and 2014 with the Nittany Lions leading the series 3-1.

Sports Illustrated: First Responder Bowl

Sports Illustrated also has the Nittany Lions traveling to the Lone Star state, but this time it’s to the home of SMU at Gerald R. Ford Stadium in University Park, Texas for the First Responder Bowl. They’re projected to face Cincinnati at 2:30 p.m. CT on Jan. 2 on ESPN.

Penn State has played the Bearcats nine times from 1981 to 2005 and holds an 8-1 series advantage. The Nittany Lions are on a seven-game winning streak, with the lone loss coming in 1983 when Penn State fell at Beaver Stadium, 14-3.

The Bearcats snapped a three-game losing streak with a 35-28 victory over Colorado on Saturday. However, they have to play No. 11 BYU to close out the regular season, so Cincinnati will likely end the year with a 6-6 record, barring an upset.

College Football News: Puerto Rico Bowl

College Football News has Penn State traveling outside the United States, projecting the Nittany Lions to face Fresno State in the debuting Puerto Rico Bowl at 1:30 p.m. on Dec. 22 at Estadio Juan Ramón Loubriel in Bayamón, home of Bayamón FC of the Liga Puerto Rico. It’ll be broadcast live on ESPN and ESPN Deportes.

This season’s bowl schedule will be historic for college football, as it will bring football to Puerto Rico for the first time. However, the Puerto Rico Bowl itself won’t be the first game played in the territory, as the San Juan Bowl is set to take place between an ACC team and a Sun Belt team on Dec. 16.

title: Penn State LB Tony Rojas named Bednarik Award Player of the Week
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
Tony Rojas was named the Bednarik Award Player of the Week after his performance against Rutgers on Saturday.

Despite the loss, Rojas had one of the best games of his career, leading Penn State in many statistical categories. He finished the day with 15 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks and two pass breakups.

Rojas has been recognized for his performance before and during the 2026 campaign, being named to the Comeback Player of the Year, Hispanic College Football Player of the Year and Lott IMPACT Trophy watch lists. He was also added to the Bednarik Award midseason watch list and was named a semifinalist for the Butkus Award.

With his performance on Saturday, Rojas became just the fourth player since 1960 to record 85-plus tackles and 15-plus tackles for loss in a season, joining Jimmy Kennedy, Dan Connor and NaVorro Bowman.

Rojas played on every defensive snap on Saturday, marking his third time in the last five games reaching that feat.

title: Penn State K Ryan Barker says he plans to return in 2027
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State's starting kicker announced his plan to return for a fifth year.

Redshirt junior Ryan Barker said Tuesday he plans to be a Nittany Lion next season because there's "only one place I'd want to play at." He did say, however, that he hasn't made an official decision.

"It's the relationships that I've made here throughout my time combined with the university itself, the Pennsylvania pipeline, local and state," Barker said Tuesday. "It's just a dream come true and with each year that's passed since I've been here it just feels like I'm living the dream more and more."

Barker currently ranks first all-time at Penn State with a 84.9% career field goal percentage. His 45 career field goals made and 98.4% extra point conversion rate both rank seventh in program history.

He broke the single-season record with a 94.7% field goal percentage last season, but has trended down this year, with four misses on 16 attempts for a 75% rate.

However, right now Barker is a perfect 37-for-37 on extra point attempts.

title: Penn State women’s volleyball rematches with Wisconsin in the Big Ten Tournament semifinals
author: Ashley Felsberg I The Daily Collegian
description:
The Nittany Lions have advanced to the Big Ten Tournament semifinals after an exciting Major League Volleyball draft night for senior Kennedy Martin and graduate student Whitney Lauenstein.

Penn State beat Illinois 3-1 on Sunday night to advance to the semifinals, this time rematching Wisconsin.

The last time the blue and white saw the Badgers was earlier this month. The Nittany Lions and the Badgers fought a competitive match; however, Penn State ultimately won in the fifth set.

Martin and long-time teammate Alexis Stucky led the Nittany Lions throughout the entire match. Martin contributed a stacked stat line, leading the blue and white in three categories: digs, aces and most notably, kills.

The 6-foot-6 senior added 28 kills, three aces and 12 digs. Along with Martin, Stucky paired her domination with 55 assists, guiding Martin and Lauenstein in creating an effective offense. Lauenstein added 15 kills and three digs of her own, making it difficult for the Badger defense to keep up.

Despite what would seem like an offensive domination, the Badgers and Nittany Lions traded set wins back and forth until the fifth set. Wisconsin took sets one and three, led by Big Ten Freshman of the Year Decelise Champion and Charlie Fuerbringer.

While the Stucky-Martin duo had them beat statistically, Champion and Fuerbringer added an impressive combined 21 kills, two aces, 25 digs and 46 assists.

The Badgers enter this match after an exciting showing against Michigan State. While the Spartans gained an early lead in their Sunday matchup, it was short-lived, as the Badgers went on to win three sets in a row to take the match.

The first three sets stayed relatively close, with neither team winning by more than a seven-point margin. However, the fourth set saw quite the opposite as the Badgers limited the Spartans to single digits, dominating 25-9.

Champion led the team with 16 kills; senior Grace Egan and freshman Audrey Flanagan followed closely, combining for 26 kills. Champion also contributed her fourth double-double of the season, contributing 11 digs throughout the match.

For the Nittany Lions to beat a 21-7 Badger squad, their blockers must find a way to shut down Champion. Lauenstein and Martin have paired well with Gabrielle Nichols and Kendall Northern all season to put up paired blocks against hearty opponents.

Northern also led the team in blocks in the Nov. 8 matchup between the two teams, with five total.

Along with Champion, Fuerbringer also poses a threat while also replicating Stucky’s craft. Fuerbringer has totaled 1,205 assists, 139 points and 26 service aces.

The Nittany Lions struggled in the first set against Wisconsin, so they must focus on execution and avoid unnecessary errors as they meet the Badgers again.

In contrast, Penn State’s offensive line of Martin, Lauenstein and Stucky poses the biggest threat to the Badgers.

Martin is coming off of a 25-kill performance against Illinois. She also contributed eight digs and hit .440. Launestein added 15 kills and five digs of her own, and Stucky put up another consistent performance, adding 48 assists.

Stucky now has 4,105 total career assists, earning her 4,000th in Penn State’s recent Nov. 14 matchup against Illinois in regular-season play

Martin and Lauenstein also, notably, had a successful Major League Volleyball draft night yesterday. Martin was the No. 1 overall first pick and was selected by the Los Angeles Thunder. Lauenstein followed immediately, selected No. 2 overall by the Las Vegas Thrill.

Aside from this earlier win, history remains on Penn State’s side, as they’ve won 19 of their 29 total meetups. Wisconsin’s last win against Penn State dates back to 2024.

Although the Nittany Lions went on to win the national championship later that season, Wisconsin ended a 15-match win streak by sweeping Penn State.

Before Penn State and Wisconsin battle at 8 p.m., No. 1 Nebraska and No. 5 Purdue will kick off the action, battling for the first Big Ten Tournament final spot.

The winners of each match will meet Wednesday at 8 p.m.

title: Penn State notebook | Matt Campbell says his team isn't mentally tough enough to play a full 60 minutes
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
After an abysmal, 25-24 loss to Rutgers on Saturday, Matt Campbell took the podium in the Beaver Stadium media room Tuesday.

Campbell gave a lot of injury updates, including regarding his running back and safety rooms, praised his senior class and talked about the team’s lack of mental toughness.

Here’s a look at what Campbell had to say.

Injury updates

Penn State was down its two starting safeties for a majority of the game against Rutgers after Zion Tracy never saw the field and Jamison Patton left late in the second quarter.

“(The) Zion situation, just very unique in terms of he was able to practice,” Campbell said. “(He) went through walk through Friday, and then just tweaked it Saturday in pregame and obviously an unfortunate situation.”

Campbell said he’ll know more about Tracy’s availability for the season finale against Maryland later this week. On the other hand, he thinks Patton will be back after he was sick last week.

“(Jamison) actually was really sick all week and really tried to go last week, missed most of the week of practice,” Campbell said. “Thought we were going to be able to get more of him, and he just wasn't able to do it.”

Campbell also talked about the status of the running backs, as Carson Hansen was ruled out on Saturday and James Peoples was carted off the field after just his second run. Like Tracy, Hansen’s status will be more clear later this week, while Peoples is out.

“I think the positive is maybe not as bad as what we initially thought, but (James) will not be available this week,” Campbell said. “We'll kind of know a little bit more about what his availability would be for a bowl game.”

Running back Cam Wallace was also dinged up last week, but led the team with 16 rushes.

Wide receiver Brett Eskildsen left early in the game after battling for a deep pass and is doubtful for Saturday. Cornerback Jahmir Joseph and defensive end Caleb Bacon are both “in the same boat” as Tracy and Hansen.

Mental toughness

Coming out of the bye week, the Nittany Lions responded to their struggles and seemingly turned their season around, but Saturday’s loss to Rutgers put a halt to that.

Campbell said Tuesday his team simply isn’t mentally tough, a fact he took accountability for.

“I think we lack a mental toughness that it takes to be the best version of us for 60 minutes,” Campbell said. “I've been saying it to be quite honest with you. I said it in fall camp before we started the season, and there is a mental maturity and a toughness that it takes to be your best. And the reality of it, those are areas that we have to grow.”

Even after Saturday’s loss, Campbell emphasized the need to stay tough to finish out the season, not just for the record at the end of the year, but for the future of the program moving forward.

“We're still not where we need to be to be where we want to go, and so the the only way I know how is you show back up today and you get back to work, you get back on the practice field, and you demand a standard,” Campbell said. “You don't waver from what you believe in and what you stand for.”

Senior class

While the Nittany Lions lost their Senior Day game against Rutgers on Saturday, Campbell had a lot of praise for the way the senior class has performed both this season and against the Scarlet Knights.

“I think what I'm really proud of, and that's what was so gut wrenching about Saturday, is man, our seniors, the guys that stepped on that field and played the game Saturday, boy, they played unbelievable,” Campbell said.

Campbell specifically highlighted Becht, Tony Rojas, right tackle Anthony Donkoh, wide receiver Chase Sowell and cornerback Audavion Collins.

Over the last few weeks, Campbell has talked about finishing the season strong for the senior class. But Tuesday, he talked about the seniors themselves fighting through their final moments despite the adversity of Saturday’s contest.

“For us to be where we're at and have fought through, what we've had to fight through, and kind of do what we've done, we wouldn't even be here without those seniors and their toughness, their mental toughness, their guts,” Campbell said. “They've been a guiding light for us to be able to even show player-driven leadership like this is what it looks like. AC Collins, what he's done for this football team. You can't ask for some better humans.”

title: Penn State notebook | DC D'Anton Lynn discusses injuries to safeties, final play against Rutgers
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
D’Anton Lynn spoke to the media on Tuesday ahead of Penn State’s final regular season game against Maryland at 3:30 p.m. Saturday.

Lynn evaluated the loss to Rutgers — including the walk-off two-point conversion — and touched on injuries in the safety room.

Here’s more on what he said.

Evaluating the upset loss to Rutgers

Tony Rojas said postgame Saturday the defense might’ve grown complacent in the second half against the Scarlet Knights. However, Lynn said he felt the game was a “dog fight” the whole way through.

“There was never a point in time where I would say we felt like we had that game,” Lynn said. “We say this every single week, you can't get bored doing the same thing over and over again.”

He did say there was an issue of stamina against Rutgers, as players were gassed out at times. However, Lynn said there’s no excuse for not doing “the little things right” despite fatigue, because the team hasn’t been able to play a complete four quarters.

“It doesn't matter if you play 80 plays, if you play 100 plays, if you're out there for a 5-yard drive or a 20-yard drive,” Lynn said. “We have a job to get off the field and regardless of the circumstances, we're not doing that enough at the end of games.”

Lynn looked back at Rutgers’ walk-off two-point conversion and said the team wasn’t aligned correctly to counter the Scarlet Knights’ formation.

He said the coaching staff stresses the importance of personal responsibility in coverage, which needs to be adjusted if the defense picks up on a disguise or alignment issue. The team didn’t do that on the game-winning play.

“They got aligned in a formation where sometimes, based off the the splits, or based off the look that the offense gives you, you have to adjust your alignment to align for success,” Lynn said. “If you can't get the job done, you need to align to where you can get the job done, and we just weren't properly aligned for that play right there.”

Injuries in the safety room

Penn State lost both of its starting safeties on Saturday when Zion Tracy got injured in pregame warmups and Jamison Patton left the game in the second quarter. Lynn said it was more difficult to lose Tracy specifically because he had practiced all week in preparation for Rutgers, but the team needed to be ready to adapt.

Patton was a game-time decision after previously being questionable on Friday’s availability report.

“(Zion’s injury) was something that kind of caught us off guard in pregame,” Lynn said. “At the end of the day, it's next man up. Everyone's in the same meetings. Everyone knows the install. With Jamison, we knew that he was going to try to play, but we knew that there was going to be a chance that he wouldn't play all game.”

That next man up was true freshman Bryson Williams, as Jeremiah Cooper and Vaboue Toure had played more snaps than Lynn expected. With Tracy and Patton banged up, Lynn said getting Williams game reps was “a great experience for him down the road.”

“Just the way the game was going, and some guys were gassed, some guys needed a break, he was the next man up,” Lynn said. “At the end of the day, (Williams) knows what to do, and we trusted him out there.”

Balancing swagger with discipline

Lynn said he wants his defensive backs to play with confidence, but he also said there’s a line the players can’t cross, as they’ve gotten into trouble with the officials.

A prime example of crossing the line was cornerback Josiah Zayas’ unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for taunting an opponent after an incompletion.

“We've gotten called on that twice now, and it's a celebration that I think every defensive back in the country does,” Lynn said. “We just need to be smarter about the direction that we're doing it. Refs are going to emphasize if you're doing it towards an opponent, then it could be taunting, so it’s something that we’ve been harping on our guys with.”

Situations like those have come on third down stops, and have given teams favorable field position on first down. Therefore, Lynn said the defense must balance playing “with edge” and not unnecessarily hurting the team.

“You want those guys to play confident and to be able to be themselves,” Lynn said. “But we have to be smart.”

title: Nittany Lions in the NFL | Saquon Barkley, Ji’Ayir Brown score in Week 11
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
While Penn State struggled against Rutgers, several former Nittany Lions had standout performances in the NFL last week.

Saquon Barkley and Ji’Ayir Brown both found the end zone, Abdul Carter and Zakee Wheatley had stat-heavy defensive performances and other players made the most of their moments.

Here's how some former Penn Staters fared in Week 11 of the NFL season.

Saquon Barkley, running back, Philadelphia Eagles

After a slow start to the season due to injury, Barkley has been consistent in scoring touchdowns each of the last four games.

Against the Pittsburgh Steelers, Barkley ran 17 times for 75 yards.

His biggest run came at the end of the first quarter, as he made three defenders miss and outran another three Steelers to find the end zone from 38 yards out.

Parker Washington, wide receiver, Jacksonville Jaguars

Washington may have experienced the biggest touchdown snub of the season against the New York Giants Sunday afternoon.

Washington ran to the back-left corner of the end zone and attempted to reel in a catch from Trevor Lawrence. It was ruled incomplete since he was bobbling the ball, although CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore and many watching believed he caught it.

Regardless, Washington still led the team with 103 receiving yards on eight catches. He was targeted 17 times in the Jacksonville Jaguars’ 23-18 loss.

Ji’Ayir Brown, safety, San Francisco 49ers

Brown became the second player on the San Francisco 49ers to record a pick six this season against Kirk Cousins, the first of which came when he was on the Las Vegas Raiders and the second with the Minnesota Vikings.

The former Nittany Lion perfectly timed his cut in front of receiver Tai Felton, intercepting the ball and returning it 18 yards for the touchdown.

Brown also had four tackles and a pass deflection in the 35-10 win on Sunday night.

Abdul Carter, linebacker, New York Giants

Last Tuesday, Carter foreshadowed his standout performance with a post on X saying, “Fast forward me to this Sunday… ima show y’all.”

He certainly showed the world his talents in a career-best outing. Carter recorded two sacks against Lawrence along with four tackles, two tackles for loss and three additional quarterback hits.

Carter had 12 total pressures, the second-most by a player in a single game this season.

Carter’s biggest play came midway through the second quarter when he came quickly off the line against tackle Walker Little. He approached Lawrence’s blindside and brought him down for a loss of six yards.

Zakee Wheatley, safety, Carolina Panthers

Although Wheatley was tied for first on the team in tackles with eight and had the most in a game in his career, he was frequently exposed in the Panthers’ 35-33 thrilling win against the Baltimore Ravens.

Wheatley was targeted frequently by quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who had 276 yards. He allowed back-to-back big gains by the Ravens, including a 34-yard pass to wide receiver Devontez Walker, followed by a 19-yard touchdown by running back Justice Hill.

Harrison Wallace III, wide receiver, Arizona Cardinals

While the Arizona Cardinals were blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday, Wallace had his best game in the NFL.

Wallace finished the day with a team-high 57 yards on four receptions, averaging 14.3 yards per catch. The Cardinals offense finished with just 205 yards in the 34-7 outing, but Wallace accounted for over a quarter of that despite having just one catch on the season heading into the game.

Mike Gesicki, tight end, Cincinnati Bengals

Gesicki and the Cincinnati Bengals didn’t emerge with a victory Monday night, but he had one of his best performances in his ninth year in the NFL.

Gesicki led the team with 77 yards and tied Ja’Marr Chase and Chase Brown with a team-high five receptions.

The former Nittany Lions’ biggest moment came in the Bengals’ final drive, when Burrow connected with him for a 32-yard pickup, ultimately leading to a field goal that gave them the lead. However, the Washington Commanders engineered a five-play, 64-yard drive to win 22-20 as time expired.

title: Recruiting roundup | Penn State earns 1st flip, other targets visit for final home game
author: Andrew Deal | Wrestling Editor
description:
Penn State’s final home game of the season was a big one on the recruiting front, and despite the bad loss to Rutgers, it’s still coming out of the weekend with success for the future.

The Nittany Lions have earned commits in back-to-back days, and there are other targets on the horizon that could pledge to them.

Here’s everything that happened on the recruiting front over the weekend.

Back-to-back commits

Penn State earned commits in two straight days — 2028 4-star cornerback Damontae Butler announced his commitment on Sunday, while 2027 3-star defensive lineman Will Zaccagnino flipped from Wisconsin to the Nittany Lions on Monday.

Matt Campbell has shown the ability to recruit in Ohio, and he proved it again with a major addition to the 2028 class in Butler.

Butler was on campus for Saturday’s game and ranks as the No. 348 player in 2028, No. 34 cornerback in his class and No. 11 player in Ohio, according to 247Sports composite. He’s also the top cornerback in Ohio for the 2028 class.

Zaccagnino was one of multiple recruits in Happy Valley over the weekend who were committed elsewhere. He’s now joined Penn State’s 2027 class, adding to the defensive line room.

He projects as a versatile player, something that both Campbell and D’Anton Lynn have harped on having on the defense. The 6-foot-5, 270-pound defensive lineman is similarly sized to current Penn State defensive end Ikenna Ezeogu, who’s 6-foot-5, 273 pounds. Ezeogu has moved around the defensive line in different packages and has rushed the passer from the inside a lot more as of late.

Zaccagnino ranks as the No. 955 player in the country, No. 115 defensive lineman and No. 3 player in Connecticut. Penn State now has two of the top six players in Connecticut on board, as he joins offensive lineman Oscar Webersink, the No. 6 player in the state.

What’s next?

After getting one of their targets in Zaccagnino, there’s still a few others who the Nittany Lions are trying to flip.

3-star Boston College quarterback commit Ben Rolapp was at Penn State beginning on Sunday. He led Brunswick School to a 41-14 championship victory over Taft on Saturday before making his way down to Pennsylvania.

He’s the No. 1521 player in the country, No. 82 quarterback and No. 9 player in Connecticut. He’d add to the growing pipeline in Connecticut that’s already in the 2027 class.

Campbell and the staff have also looked to add at wide receiver. 3-star James Madison commit Donte Dent Jr. visited for Penn State’s Senior Day, ranking as the No. 1027 player in the 2027 class, No. 64 athlete and No. 25 player in Virginia.

He has the build of the new Penn State receivers, especially under wide receivers coach Kashif Moore. Standing at 6-foot-4, Dent would bring a big-bodied receiver to the class and the team.

Another weak spot in the class, a Louisville linebacker commit was in town for the Nittany Lions’ final game. 3-star Josiah Pouncy visited as Penn State looks to add to its one linebacker pledge in the 2027 class.

Pouncy is the No. 634 player in the class, No. 47 linebacker and No. 24 player in Ohio out of the Cincinnati area. Pouncy goes to North College Hill High School, just 11 miles south of where 3-star 2027 running back commit Jordan Hall plays at Princeton High School.

2028 class visitors

Alongside now-2028 commit Butler and longtime cornerback commit Deonte Flemings Jr., Penn State also had some other highly ranked players in attendance.

4-star running back Cartae Ligon visited the Nittany Lions for the first time. A 2028 recruit, he’s made his way around the country this year, with visits to Ohio State, Indiana, North Carolina and Kentucky.

Additionally, 4-star athlete Brandon Murphy Jr. was in Beaver Stadium for the second straight week. He’s the No. 9 athlete in the 2028 class and No. 4 player in Pennsylvania.

Penn State welcomed four players from a top-10 Virginia high school, Green Run. 4-star edge rusher Qwayvon Cleveland, 3-star edge rusher Junious Clay, 3-star linebacker Corvin Watson and defensive lineman Saleh Robinson Jr. were all on a visit together.

The Nittany Lions will likely have to battle with James Franklin and Virginia Tech for Cleveland and Clay, who are the higher ranked of the four teammates.

title: Penn State women's volleyball makes MLV Draft history, Las Vegas Thrill select Whitney Lauenstein
author: Ashley Felsberg I The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State just made history.

Outside hitter Whitney Lauenstein was drafted No. 2 overall by the Las Vegas Thrill in the MLV Draft after a last-minute trade.

The Thrill selected Lauenstein after swapping picks with the Los Angeles Thunder to pave the way for her teammate Kennedy Martin to be drafted No. 1 overall — the first back-to-back leadoff selection of college teammates in MLV.

The Las Vegas Thrill makes their return next year after having to pause operations during the 2026 season to find stable ownership.

Lauenstein is currently with the Nittany Lions in Fishers, Indiana, along with Martin, competing in the first-ever Big Ten tournament. They will be playing the tournament semifinals Wednesday night against Wisconsin.

Lauenstein has played for three programs throughout her career. The Waverly, Nebraska, native started her collegiate career with the Cornhuskers for two seasons. In her freshman year, Lauenstein played in a total of 67 sets, adding 62 kills, 24 digs, and 22 blocks to the Cornhuskers’ stat line.

In her sophomore year in Lincoln, the outside hitter appeared in 107 sets, adding 114 blocks, 99 digs, 28 aces, and 297 kills, while earning AVCA All-Region honors and selection to the Academic All-Big Ten Team.

After concluding her 2022 season at Nebraska, Launestein took time off to welcome a daughter and eventually transferred to Texas to represent the Longhorns for two seasons.

In her junior year, she only appeared in two matches and totaled three sets, but was able to contribute a dig and a block each, along with three kills. In her final year with the Longhorns, Lauenstein appeared in 20 sets, adding 33 kills, 14 blocks and 11 digs to the stat line.

Lauenstein didn’t join Penn State until her fifth year of eligibility. Currently, she has earned season highs of 19 kills, 21.5 points, three aces and nine kills in her final collegiate season.

title: Penn State women’s volleyball's Kennedy Martin selected No. 1 in MLV Draft by Los Angeles Thunder
author: Ashley Felsberg I The Daily Collegian
description:
A current Nittany Lion has been drafted to Major League Volleyball.

Penn State right-side hitter Kennedy Martin was selected No. 1 overall by the Los Angeles Thunder in the MLV Draft. The Thunder originally had the second overall selection, but traded with the Las Vegas Thrill to select Martin.

The Thrill went on to select her Penn State teammate, Whitney Lauenstein, with the next pick. The Los Angeles Thunder are one of the new MLV expansion teams for next year.

Martin was drafted, but she’s also currently representing the Nittany Lions at the first-ever Big Ten Tournament in Fishers, Indiana.

Martin also has the option to return to Penn State for her fifth year due to the NCAA Five-for-Five Eligibility Rule, although she's not announced that decision. Martin was asked about her options and the possibility of going pro on the draft's broadcast.

"I'm just super honored to be selected," Martin said. "What's going on in the pro leagues right now has been really amazing to see and to see it being built up through my earlier years of college, so I'm really honored to be selected."

Martin’s season highs this year include 34 kills, 15 digs, four aces, seven total blocks, and 35.5 points in a game, and the rest of her collegiate career has been just as successful.

The South Carolina native originally started her career at Florida, where she stayed for two seasons, before joining former and now current teammate Alexis Stucky in Happy Valley.

Throughout her time at Florida, Martin totaled 1,004 kills, 18 assists and 356 digs in 205 total sets. Her freshman year, she was selected as a second-team AVCA All-American, made the AVCA All-Southeast Region First Team, and made the All-SEC First Team. She was also named AVCA National Division I Player of the Week, SEC Player of the Week twice, SEC Freshman of the Week, and named an SEC All-American Freshman.

In her sophomore year in Gainesville, Martin earned first-team AVCA All-American and first-team CSC Academic All-American honors. She was also named AVCA Southeast Region Player of the Year and an AVCA Division I Player of the Year semifinalist. Martin led the nation in points per set and was named AVCA National Division I Player of the Week, five-time SEC Player of the Week, and a member of the CSC Academic All-District Team.

Since joining the Nittany Lions, Martin has been named Big Ten Player of the Year and is currently a semifinalist for National Player of the Year. This is the second time Martin has been a semifinalist for this award.

Martin was also a three-time Big Ten Player of the Week, an AVCA National Division I Player of the Week, and made the AVCA All-East Coast Region Team and All-Big Ten First Team in her junior year.

Coach Katie Schumacher-Cawley has watched for two years as Martin has added 1,121 kills, 36 assists, and 489 digs to the blue and white stat line, all in 216 total sets - and counting.

Martin leads the Big Ten in points and kills as she guides her team through the rest of the Big Ten Tournament this week and waits to make an NCAA Tournament push.

title: Big Ten roundup | Major upsets create chaos in Week 12
author: Andrew Deal | Wrestling Editor
description:
As crazy as the college football season has been, the Big Ten’s top teams had managed to avoid the major upsets throughout most of the year.

That changed in Week 12, with three ranked teams falling to upsets, including two top-10 teams losing in overtime. However, Iowa and USC continued to win, hanging around the middle of the College Football Playoff rankings.

Here’s how the hectic Big Ten slate went down.

Nebraska gets historic upset win

Despite Ohio State having three losses, it was still in a position to backdoor its way into the College Football Playoff.

However, those hopes disappeared as Nebraska pulled off the upset, one that’ll go down in history. The Cornhuskers won their first game against a ranked opponent since 2016 after losing 31 straight contests to them. It was also Nebraska’s first win against Ohio State since 2011.

The Cornhuskers controlled most of the game, but a third quarter touchdown from the Buckeyes tied things up at 21. However, a five-play drive set up a field goal for Nebraska to take a 24-21 lead to begin the fourth quarter.

An interception from Ohio State quarterback Luke Fahey set up the Cornhuskers to go up two scores again, and Nebraska quarterback Anthony Colandrea sealed the deal with a touchdown pass to wide receiver Quinn Clark from 26 yards out.

Even with a rushing touchdown from the Buckeyes’ running back Bo Jackson, it was too little too late as Nebraska ran the rest of the clock out and stormed the field after the upset.

UCLA, Indiana fall in overtime

Both Indiana and UCLA have been escaping with victories and have pretty similar situations. The Bruins have been working with backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach after Nico Iamaleava went down with a season-ending injury, while Indiana has been rotating quarterbacks, with starter Josh Hoover struggling to stay healthy enough to play.

On Saturday, the winning ways came crashing down within minutes of each other. UCLA went to overtime with Michigan, as the Bruins’ offense struggled to sustain any rhythm against the Wolverines’ stout defense. To make matters worse, Dieffenbach left the game with an injury in overtime, and UCLA had to rely on freshman quarterback Madden Iamaleava to try to pull out the win.

Knotted up at 16 after back-to-back field goals from each team, UCLA was unsuccessful on its touchdown attempt from the 3-yard line. Michigan responded with a pass from Bryce Underwood to tight end Jalen Hoffman to convert the two-point conversion and take down the Bruins, 18-16.

Indiana traveled to Washington and maintained either a tie or lead for most of the game after a one-play touchdown from Grant Wilson to Charlie Becker tied things up at 7-7.

Washington scored with three minutes left in the game to tie it, 24-24. The Huskies received the ball first in overtime and settled for a field goal to take a 27-24 lead, their first lead of the game since their touchdown drive to open the game.

The Hoosiers had a chance to respond, and after a third-and-11 completion for seven yards, they lined up for a game-tying field goal to move to a second overtime. Kicker Paddy McAteer’s attempt hooked wide left and the Huskies pulled off the third upset in the Big Ten on the same day.

During the game, Wilson was benched for Josh Hoover, and Curt Cignetti said Monday they’ll both take reps with the ones this week.

Iowa, USC keep playoff hopes alive

While all three of Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA fell on Saturday, two other Big Ten ranked squads won to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive.

Iowa traveled to Illinois to take on the Fighting Illini, and the Hawkeyes pulled away despite being tied 17-17 at the half. They shut out Illinois in the second half, 17-0, behind a rushing touchdown from quarterback Hank Brown and a pick six by defensive back Jaylen Watson.

Running back L.J. Phillips Jr. had an impressive day on the ground, rushing for 154 yards and a touchdown.

No. 18 USC hosted Maryland before its rivalry-week game against UCLA. Similarly, it was a close game in the first half with the Terrapins leading 14-13 at the break.

The Trojans turned things on in the second half with two rushing touchdowns from running back Waymond Jordan, who led the team with 70 rushing yards in the 35-21 win over Maryland.

Both USC and Iowa will move up in the updated rankings, and still are in a spot to potentially slide into the College Football Playoff if other teams in front of them falter.

title: Penn State women’s hockey earns 2 AHA weekly honors
author: Noah Radio | The Daily Collegian
description:
After two blowout victories over Delaware, Grace Outwater and Kylie Amelkovich earned Atlantic Hockey America awards for forward of the week and rookie of the week, respectively.

Outwater, a junior captain, scored two goals and assisted on two more in the series. The Picton, Ontario, native moved to fourth on Penn State’s career goals list with 51.

As for the newcomer, Amelkovich led the blue and white with six points across the two matchups. She racked up four assists on Thursday, then added another on Friday and netted a goal of her own. The Glen Ellyn, Illinois, native was also dominant in the circle, winning 30 of 36 faceoffs in the series.

Outwater, Amelkovich and the Nittany Lions are back in action for a pair of neutral site games in Washington D.C. this weekend against Boston College and Minnesota. The puck drops against the Eagles at 5 p.m. on Friday.

title: Penn State picks up commitment from 2027 3-star Will Zaccagnino
author: Andrew Mercer | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State has flipped a defensive lineman commit from a conference opponent.

The Nittany Lions flipped 3-star Wisconsin defensive lineman commit Will Zaccagnino on Monday, he announced via X.

Zaccagnino is the No. 3 player out of Connecticut and the No. 115 defensive lineman in the nation, according to 247Sports composite.

With a 6-foot-5, 270-pound frame, Zaccagnino committed to Wisconsin on April 30.

He plays both defensive end and offensive lineman for St. Joseph’s in his hometown of Trumbull, Connecticut, tallying 25 tackles, nine quarterback hurries, five tackles for loss, two sacks and a blocked punt.

title: No. 7 Penn State women’s volleyball takes down Illinois in Big Ten Tournament quarterfinals
author: Jimmy Blair | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State entered the inaugural Big Ten tournament as the second-ranked team in the conference, behind only Nebraska. The Nittany Lions earned a double bye, making their tournament debut a quarterfinal matchup with No. 7-seeded Illinois.

Additionally, Penn State looked to continue its strong momentum after winning its last 10 games of the regular season.

The blue and white got its 11th consecutive win, defeating the Fighting Illini 3-1, with Big Ten Player of the Year Kennedy Martin putting up 25 kills.

Katie Schumacher-Cawley looked to continue to take advantage of the team’s talent to make a run in the conference tournament before the run for the national championship.

Martin got the blue and white on the board with her first two kills of the tournament coming back-to-back.

The Fighting Illini went out to a small lead early, but a hard shot to the back right corner by Whitney Lauenstein made it a 9-8 match.

Illinois kept the pressure up throughout the beginning of the opening set, but another kill from Gabrielle Nichols followed by an ace from Alexis Stucky put the blue and white up 13-12 going into the first stoppage.

Consistent big rallies became the story of the first set, as the Fighting Illini kept taking points by pushing back against the Nittany Lions’ offensive attack. Paityn Chapman continued beating the Nittany Lion back line from the right side, helping Illinois out to an 18-15 lead.

The Fighting Illini took the first set off a service ace from Chapman. This marked the first time since Nov. 8 against Wisconsin that the blue and white dropped the first set.

Illinois kept the momentum going to begin the second set, but a block at the net by Martin gave the blue and white some momentum back, taking the next four points.

Emmi Sellman notched a kill for an 8-5 Penn State lead, as the blue and white began to attack the open space in the middle of Illinois’ formation.

Illinois responded with an 8-2 scoring run to take a 13-11 lead. The Nittany Lions took a timeout, then won the next four points, making the score 15-13 in favor of Penn State.

Both sides went back and forth as the second set continued, with Illinois taking a timeout with the blue and white leading 19-16.

Illinois put up a fight at the end of the set, but Martin’s 10th kill of the match clinched the second set for the blue and white, tying the match at one set apiece.

Martin picked up right where she left off with another kill to start set three. The blue and white got out to a 4-1 lead following an unsuccessful challenge from Illinois.

Haley Burgdorf committed an attack error, then immediately responded with a kill. This mirrored how Schumacher-Cawley’s side continued to consistently respond when Illinois took a point.

The blue and white took a 15-9 lead following an attack error from Illinois’ Maya Harris. Both sides continued playing elite team defense, causing the long rallies to continue.

Illinois’ defense began to take over the match, as the Fighting Illini took three straight points, making the score 19-16. Once again, the blue and white answered with a run of its own, resulting in a set-point scenario. A kill from Nichols clinched a crucial third set for the blue and white.

Illinois opened the fourth set with back-to-back points, but the Nittany Lions answered with four points of their own. Another run from Illinois put it up 9-7, causing Penn State to call a timeout.

Both sides traded blows as the fourth set continued. The Nittany Lions took five of six points to take a 15-13 lead going into the media break. Martin continued to rack up kills as both sides went back and forth.

Despite sound defense from the Fighting Illini, the blue and white stood its ground defensively as well, converting those chances into points, as it has done all season. In addition, Penn State dominated the net in the fourth set, punishing Illinois with blocks.

A block by Kendall Northern secured the win for the Nittany Lions after four sets, advancing to the semifinals.

Up Next

The Nittany Lions will face the winner of Michigan State versus Wisconsin in the semifinals on Tuesday at 8 p.m. ET.

MORE VOLLEYBALL COVERAGE

title: Week 12 report card | Penn State falls apart in devastating loss to Rutgers
author: Noah Aberegg | The Daily Collegian
description:
Penn State’s loss to Rutgers is a game that many players and fans would like to forget.

The matchup featured standout performances from wide receiver Chase Sowell and Tony Rojas, but otherwise, it was an overall poor performance from the Nittany Lions.

Here’s how I’d grade each part of Penn State’s loss to the Scarlet Knights.

Overall: D

Coaching staff: F

Before Saturday’s loss, it had been 38 years since Rutgers beat the Nittany Lions and 32 years since it last scored a touchdown in Beaver Stadium. Penn State fell apart as the offense failed to convert on short-yardage situations, and the defense couldn’t adjust to quick passes in the flat.

After the contest, Matt Campbell said, “I didn’t have us prepared to play our best football game, Senior Day, the end of the season, and that really hurts me.”

Offense: C

The Nittany Lions put up 24 points on Saturday, which could win a game depending on the circumstances. But they were playing against the worst defense in the conference, so the performance was underwhelming.

Pass game: B+

Rocco Becht delivered through the air with 233 yards and a touchdown to Sowell, who finished the day with 123 yards on six catches. Freshman Zay Robinson also had a standout day with three receptions for 54 yards as Brett Eskildsen was sidelined with an injury early on.

However, the lack of usage from the tight ends was an issue, as Benjamin Brahmer and Andrew Rappleyea combined for just four catches for 44 yards. Gabe Burkle did not record a reception.

Run game: D

Cam Wallace started strong in the absence of Carson Hansen, rushing for a 56-yard touchdown to cap off the second drive. After James Peoples was carted to the locker room early on, Wallace continued to take a bulk of the carries.

He struggled in short-yardage situations, as Penn State was 0-for-2 on fourth down and 4-for-10 on third down with a majority of the failed conversions coming as run plays. Not being able to extend drives proved to hinder the Nittany Lions’ chances of coming out victorious, especially considering the Scarlet Knights allowed the most rushing yards per game in the Big Ten entering Saturday’s contest.

Offensive line: C+

Penn State’s offensive line gave up two sacks to the Scarlet Knights, who forced Becht to scramble often, and struggled to create gaps in the second half. However, they had a few good blocks in the run game, including when Cooper Cousins and Trevor Buhr ran a pin and pull on Wallace’s 56-yard score.

Defense: C-

Rutgers was playing its second-string quarterback AJ Surace, who had three broken ribs and didn’t throw a football all week. Surace finished the day with 178 yards, while running back Antwan Raymond ran for 101 yards.

Pass rush: B+

The Nittany Lions took down Surace four times on Saturday, as Rojas added to his season total with 1.5 more sacks. Alex McPherson, Ike Ezeogu and Armstrong Nnodim all contributed as well.

Secondary: D

Penn State was forced to play its backup safeties as Zion Tracy tweaked something before the game and Jamison Patton left mid-game due to injury. Jeremiah Cooper and Vaboue Toure had to play their most snaps of the season, which Rutgers took advantage of.

Cornerback Josiah Zayas was also targeted down the final stretch, as he gave up a pair of crucial plays on the scoring drive. He was also called for taunting, which ultimately led to a touchdown, and Audavion Collins and Daryus Dixson were called for pass interference on the last drive.

Linebackers: C-

It’s hard to give the linebackers such a low grade considering Rojas’ big-time performance. Kooper Ebel once again struggled to tackle and couldn’t bring down Raymond on the eventual touchdown.

Special teams: A-

The special teams unit was the best aspect of the game against Rutgers. Ryan Barker made both his extra points, while punter Nathan Tiyce pinned two of his four punts inside the 20-yard line.

Tiyce’s final punt went for only 31 yards and gave the Scarlet Knights good field position to set up their game-winning drive.

title: Penn State wrestling has perfect 8 champions in C.J. Morgan Invitational
author: The Daily Collegian wrestling staff
description:
Penn State sent 16 wrestlers to the newly named C.J. Morgan Invitational at West Point, New York.

The formerly named Army Black Knight Invitational has been a yearly showcase of the Nittany Lions’ depth at different weight classes. The 2026 edition was no different, as they had wrestlers win the title in all eight weight classes where they had representatives.

Here’s how the wrestlers did.

125 pounds

Quarterfinals: No. 1 Luke Lilledahl (PSU) vs. Waylon Rodgers (VMI)

Lilledahl routed Rodgers in an 18-3 tech fall victory, notching four takedowns and two near falls to secure the victory. Lilledahl only needed two periods to do so, as the junior continued his undefeated season at his first open tournament of the year.

Semifinals: Luke Lilledahl (PSU) vs. Teague Strobel (HOF)

Lilledahl once again outclassed his opponent, winning by 19-4 tech fall. The St. Charles, Missouri, native secured six takedowns and an escape in the victory, pushing him to the championship match.

Finals: Luke Lilledahl (PSU) vs. Cadell Lee (ARMY)

Lilledahl outclassed Lee in his 20-5 tech fall win. Lilledahl only scored one takedown in the first period, but the following rounds separated him. Five takedowns, an escape and a riding time point gave Lilledahl enough to secure the championship win at 125.

133 pounds

Round of 16: Nate Desmond (PSU) vs Caleb Uhorchuk (ARMY)

Desmond wrestled a shutout against Uhorchuk in his first bout of the year. The redshirt freshman notched a takedown along with three four-point nearfalls to make it through the first round with a 15-0 tech-fall win.

Quarterfinals: Nate Desmond (PSU) vs Kyle Gibson (VMI)

Desmond suffered what seemed to be a knee injury after reaching for his knee, only four seconds into the match, causing him to forfeit.

Quarterfinals: No. 16 Masanosuke Ono (PSU) vs Gauge Shipp (HOF)

Ono continued the common trend within his matches, coming out hot to start the first period. Ono earned a 13-7 lead after the initial three minutes. The other side of the trend is his tendency to fizzle out, which occurred yet again in his 19-9 major decision victory.

Semifinals: No. 16 Masanosuke Ono (PSU) vs No. 30 Joseph Uhorchuk (ARMY)

Ono faced the brother of Desmond's first opponent, and both relatives suffered the same outcome. The Matsue City, Japan, native scored three takedowns in the first period, and let his foot off the gas in the latter periods by only tallying an escape point. He came out with a 10-3 decision to advance to the finals.

Championship: No. 16 Masanosuke Ono (PSU) vs Evin Gursoy (COL)

Ono notched two takedowns early in the first period to take a 6-2 lead, continuing his trend of fast starts. While no points were scored in the second period, Ono earned an escape point in the third.

Ono’s seven points were enough to crown him the champion of the 133-pound division following his 7-2 win.

141 pounds

Round of 16: No. 3 Marcus Blaze (PSU) vs Phoenix Alyea (VMI)

Blaze cruised through his first opponent of the day. Blaze tallied two takedowns and a four-point near fall, holding a 10-1 lead, before pinning Alyea with less than a minute left in the first period.

Quarterfinals: Marcus Blaze (PSU) vs Brady Kaupp (COL)

Blaze continued his dominant run through the bracket with a 17-1 tech-fall win over Kaupp. Blaze racked up three takedowns and two four-point near falls while only allowing one escape in the process.

Semifinals: Marcus Blaze (PSU) vs Kyison Garcia (PSU)

Blaze got the best of Garcia in the meeting between two Nittany Lions in the tournament. Blaze dominated in a 23-7 tech fall victory, notching seven takedowns and a reversal. Garcia’s only points were via escapes, which he scored on every one of Blaze’s takedowns.

Championship: No. 3 Marcus Blaze (PSU) vs No. 22 Braden Basile (ARMY)

Blaze took Basile to the ground four times in the first period, building his lead to 12-3. Blaze finished the job with two takedowns and an escape point to seal his championship win with a 19-4 score.

Quarterfinals: Kyison Garcia (PSU) vs Conor Collins (ARMY)

Garcia posted his first win of the season, defeating Collins 7-1 in a decision. He scored two takedowns and an escape in a low-scoring affair. The senior held his lead for the entirety of the match.

Consolations Semifinals: Hayden Cunningham (PSU) vs. Kyison Garcia (PSU)

Cunningham got the best of his teammate in a 5-4 decision win. Garcia held the lead heading into the third period, notching a takedown while Cunningham took two escapes. Yet, Cunningham stole a takedown with 50 seconds left in the third period to close out the bout.

Fifth place: Kyison Garcia (PSU) vs. Scotty Johnson (BLOOM)

Garcia finished his tournament with a fifth-place finish following his 12-6 win. Garcia once again entered the third period with a 5-3 deficit. Garcia wrestled a phenomenal stretch, earning two knockdowns, an escape point, and a riding time point.

Quarterfinals: Hayden Cunningham (PSU) vs Braden Basile (ARMY)

Cunningham continued to have a rough start to the season, taking his second loss of the season. The Nittany Lion was down 7-4 at the 45-second mark of the second period before losing via pinfall to Basile.

Consolations of 4: Hayden Cunningham (PSU) vs. Chris Lalonde (VMI)

Cunningham made it look easy as he pinned Lalonde in the first period to secure the win. He had already built a 16-0 lead beforehand, consisting of a take down and four near falls. With the win, Cunningham advanced to the third-place bout.

Third place: Hayden Cunningham (PSU) vs. Roman Lermer (COL)

Cunningham could not score a point in his 3-0 loss against Lermer, settling for fourth place in the bracket. Lermer’s lone takedown in the first period was enough to take the win.

149 pounds

Quarterfinals: Brock Weiss (PSU) vs Mason Barvitskie (ARMY)

Weiss added himself to the short list of Nittany Lions to begin the season with a loss, as he fell to Barvitskie by an 8-2 decision. A reversal in the first period was the only source of points that Weiss could generate.

Consolation of 4: Brock Weiss vs EJ Sheeran

Weiss built a commanding lead in the first period, earning two takedowns and a four-point nearfall while allowing an escape. The following period would add to the advantage, scoring two more takedowns. His final point came from riding time, as Weiss ended his day with a 17-5 major decision.

Consolation Semifinals: Brock Weiss (PSU) vs Shane Reilly (ARMY)

Weiss recorded one takedown in every period during this matchup, which was all he needed to win. Weiss did not allow a single point through the match, pitching a 10-0 shutout in the consolation match.

Quarterfinals: Dalton Perry (PSU) vs Lincoln Kelley (VMI)

The redshirt freshman made a statement in his debut match this season. Perry outclassed Kelley in a 17-2 tech fall victory. He put up four takedowns and a four-point near-fall while only allowing two escapes.

Semifinals: Dalton Perry (PSU) vs Shane Reilly (ARMY)

Perry maintained his dominant run in the bracket with an 18-1 tech fall win to advance to the championship match. Perry only needed two periods to secure three takedowns and two nearfalls, while allowing one escape point.

Finals: Dalton Perry (PSU) vs. No. 22 Lorenzo Frezza (COL)

Perry finished a great run with an 8-2 win to earn a first-place finish. Perry only picked up two takedowns during the match, but he defended Frezza’s attacks enough to prevent points outside of an escape and stalling.

157 pounds

Round of 16: No. 2 Tyler Kasak (PSU) vs Chase Hontz (HOF)

Kasak dominated in the first round of the bracket, as he’s the second Penn State wrestler to shut out his opponent at the C.J. Morgan Invitational. Kasak secured the 15-0 victory with a takedown, two two-point near falls, and two four-point near falls.

Quarterfinals: Tyler Kasak (PSU) vs Eric Alderfer (BLOOM)

Kasak followed up his first-round performance with a close win against Alderfer, who didn’t compete in Penn State’s dual meet against Bloomsburg. Kasak earned a point from two stalling calls on Alderfer, as well as a reversal, to win the low-action outing.

Semifinals: Tyler Kasak (PSU) vs. Joe Antonio (ARMY)

Kasak pinned Antonio in the first period to advance to the championship. Kasak registered a takedown before ending the bout with a win.

Finals: Tyler Kasak (PSU) vs. Connor Pierce (PSU)

The Penn State teammates met in the championship in a close, hard-fought battle. Heading into the third period, Pierce held a 1-0 lead due to an escape point. Kasak took the lead with an escape and a takedown, but Pierce fought back to earn a point in the same manner. He brought riding time under a minute to hold onto a decision.

Pierce pulled off the upset with a 5-4 decision to earn himself first place in the bracket.

Quarterfinals: Connor Pierce (PSU) vs Zach Reilley (HOF)

Pierce jumped up to 157 pounds, pinning Reilley in less than two minutes of action to send him to the next round of the bracket. Pierce notched two takedowns and a four-point near fall before the pin in his first win of the season.

Semifinals: Connor Pierce (PSU) vs Michael Turi (BLOOM)

Pierce advanced to the championship with a 12-3 victory over Michael Turi, who’s now suffered two losses to Penn State wrestlers. Pierce tallied three takedowns and an escape point, along with an escape and riding time point. He advanced to the finals in a weight class jump after consistently wrestling at 149 pounds.

174 pounds

Round of 16: No. 1 Mitchell Mesenbrink (PSU) vs Matthew Waddell (HOF)

Mesenbrink scored 23 points in his win against Waddell. The Hodge Trophy winner only needed one period to score five takedowns, a four-point near-fall, and a three-point near-fall in his tech-fall victory.

Quarterfinals: Mitchell Mesenbrink (PSU) vs Beau Lewis (VMI)

Mesenbrink earned his second tech fall win of the tournament with a score of 17-2. Mesenbrink made quick work of his opponent, securing three takedowns and two four-point near falls all within two minutes of the bout.

Semifinals: Mitchell Mesenbrink (PSU) vs Gunner Filipowicz (ARMY)

Mesenbrink continued to finish his matches early, pinning Filipowicz within less than a minute of action. Mesenbrink earned three points for the takedown that led to the pin.

Finals: Joe Sealey (PSU) vs Mitchell Mesenbrink (PSU)

Sealey’s impressive run came to an end, as he ran into arguably the best pound-for-pound wrestler in the country. Mesenbrink led after the first period with a 6-1 advantage after scoring two knockdowns.

Sealey couldn’t find any source of offense, and Mesenbrink secured one final takedown before pinning Sealey. Mesenbrink took home first place, while Sealey sat second.

Round of 16: Joe Sealey (PSU) vs Cole Pangborn (ARMY)

Sealey began his string of excellent offensive performances with a 21-6 tech fall win against Pangborn. The junior took over during the second period, with five takedowns in the span of a minute.

Quarterfinals: Joe Sealey (PSU) vs Lindson Turner (COL)

Sealey tallied three takedowns in both the first and second periods of the bout. With an 18-4 lead, all Sealey needed to do was push for another takedown, which he did with a minute left in the match. Sealey won his second tech-fall victory of the day with a score of 21-5.

Semifinals: Joe Sealey (PSU) vs Frank Volpe (HOF)

Sealey earned two takedowns to take a 6-1 lead in the opening period. Yet, Sealey built his lead in the following period, where he secured five takedowns during the final two minutes to advance to the championship match. Sealey ultimately won via 21-6 tech fall.

184 pounds

Quarterfinals: Asher Cunningham (PSU) vs Cooper Haase

Cunningham received a bye in the tournament’s opening round and began his Sunday with a 21-3 technical fall over Haase. He took the Army 184-pounder down early in the first period and worked to two sets of four near-fall points to hold an 11-0 edge after three minutes.

Haase took the Nittany Lion down to start the second frame, but Cunningham escaped and returned with a takedown of his own before six third-period back points secured the technical fall.

Semifinals: Asher Cunningham vs Nash Banko (ARMY)

Facing off against another Army wrestler in the semifinal, Cunningham made quick work of Banko to advance to the final. He took down the Black Knight early and used three sets of four near-fall points to cruise to a 15-0 tech fall in the final moments of the opening frame.

Finals: Asher Cunningham (PSU) vs Gage LaPlante (ARMY)

LaPlante scored an early first-period takedown that Cunningham was quickly able to escape. He took down Cunningham again with 18 seconds to go in the first period, though Cunningham got back to his feet to end the frame with a 6-2 advantage for LaPlante.

Cunningham started on bottom and worked to his feet before scoring his first takedown of the match, then earning four near-fall points near the end of the second frame. LaPlante chose to start the final period in neutral, and neither wrestler earning a point in the last two minutes handed Cunningham a 10-6 decision to close his afternoon.

285 pounds

Quarterfinals: No. 19 Connor Mirasola (PSU) vs Tristen Hitchcock (ARMY)

Mirasola took Hitchcock down three times in the first period, allowing the Army wrestler to stand back up each time.

Starting the second period on the bottom, he reversed position on Hitchcock and notched another pair of takedowns before bringing him to the mat a final time in the third period to claim the 21-6 tech fall.

Semifinals: Connor Mirasola (PSU) vs Elijah Brown (PSU)

The pair of Nittany Lions’ opening wins set them on a collision course in the heavyweight semifinal. Mirasola took Brown down twice in the opening period before starting the second on the bottom.

He escaped and took Brown down twice more, then earning a fifth takedown and four near-fall points in the third period to defeat his teammate in a 20-4 tech fall to advance to the final.

Finals: Connor Mirasola (PSU) vs Lucas Stoddard (ARMY)

Mirasola took Stoddard down with a minute to go in the first period, but surrendered an escape and a takedown late in the frame to trail 4-3 after three minutes. Starting on bottom, Mirasola escaped early in the second frame to level the score before scoring a late takedown to go up 7-4.

Stoddard escaped to begin the final period, but Mirasola scored three takedowns and three back points in the final two minutes to claim the title with a 19-7 major decision.

Quarterfinals: Elijah Brown (PSU) vs Charles Weidman (ARMY)

Brown opened his college career in dominant fashion, taking down Weidman in nine seconds before riding the Army redshirt freshman to 12 near-fall points for a 15-0 first-period tech fall.

Consolation Semifinals: Elijah Brown (PSU) vs. Braxton Lewis (VMI)

Brown earned a quick three points with a takedown 35 seconds into the match and rode Lewis for nearly a minute until the Keydet escaped near the midpoint of the opening period. The freshman Nittany Lion started the second frame on top, and surrendered another point when Lewis escaped early in the frame.

Nursing a slight edge, Brown opened the third period on the bottom and escaped with less than a minute to go in the match, sealing a 4-2 win to advance to the third-place match.

Third place: Elijah Brown (PSU) vs. No. 15 Vincent Mueller (COL)

Mueller took Brown down 24 seconds into the match and worked from the top for two minutes, ultimately turning the freshman heavyweight to his back and pinning him at the 2:41 mark in the first period.

Quarterfinals: Dawson Bundy vs Lucas Stoddard (ARMY)

Bundy and Stoddard battled to open the match, with the first point coming on a second-period escape from the Black Knight. Bundy started on the bottom to start the third period and escaped to level the score at 1-1, but a late Stoddard takedown and riding time point saw Bundy fall in a 5-1 decision.

Consolation of 8: Dawson Bundy (PSU) vs. Billy McChesney (COL)

Bundy was taken down early in the opening period, but returned to his feet after 20 seconds to earn his first point. McChesney escaped from the bottom to start the second period, and was issued a stalling warning before Bundy scored a takedown to level the match at 4-4.

The Nittany Lion immediately took the lead with an escape in the final frame, but surrendered a late takedown to fall 7-5 and end his tournament.
