title: State College dominates in District 6 Regional Championship victory over McDowell
author: Joey Bolger | For the Collegian
description:
The State College Little Lions football program is widely known as one of Pennsylvania’s most successful and consistent programs in high school football, under the leadership of head coach Matt Lintal.

Now in his twelfth season at the helm, Lintal has taken a historically successful program to new heights, winning 11 district titles.

This season has been no different; the Little Lions finished the regular season with a Mid-Penn Commonwealth conference title and a perfect 10-0 record, six of which were shutouts.

State College has not missed a beat heading into the 6A PIAA playoffs, shutting out Erie 55-0 in the first round. Quarterback Connor Kulka threw for 226 yards and four touchdowns; wide receiver AJ Fry caught five passes for 130 yards and four touchdowns.

Now in the second round, the Little Lions welcomed the McDowell Trojans to Memorial Stadium. State College has beaten the Trojans by multiple possessions in their previous two matchups.

McDowell walked it off in double overtime last week against the Altoona Mountain Lions with a 10-yard rushing touchdown from Chase Carrick. Quarterback Evan Kuhn threw for 399 yards and five touchdowns; Kuhn also kept it on the ground, rushing for 74 yards and adding two more touchdowns to his total.

Tonight continued State College’s streak over McDowell as the Little Lions dominated once again, taking home a 46-14 win. This marks the end of the Trojans' 26-27 campaign, while State College keeps its season alive and will take on Williamsport in the next round.

On the first drive, State College fed running back Rowan Walker the whole way, and McDowell had no answer as Walker took it into the end zone after a five-minute drive, giving the Little Lions an early 7-0 lead.

The Walker show continued throughout the entire game as he rushed for 166 yards and found himself in the end zone two more times by the end of the night.

“Rowan and AJ really do a tremendous job; they find ways to just make plays even when there’s nothing there,” said Lintal. “But they do what they’re coached to do.”

Fry was a defensive nightmare for McDowell tonight; the Old Dominion commit picked off Kuhn twice in the second quarter, taking both all the way to the house.

Along with a 38-yard strike from Kulka to wide receiver Max Vendemia, the Little Lions went into halftime with a commanding 36-7 lead.

State College’s defense shined, holding an explosive McDowell offense to only 14 points. They controlled the trenches from start to finish, giving the Trojans’ backfield barely enough time to breathe.

“Our defensive staff prepared our kids extremely well, and the kids executed the game plan,” said Lintal. “That’s a really good football team that we were able to come out on top.”

After halftime, McDowell showed a little fight early on in the third quarter as Kuhn found Taylor Lincoln on the side of the end zone, giving the Trojans their second score of the night.

The second half was quieter than the first, but the same theme continued, as the Little Lions marked their twelfth win of the season and advanced to the next round.

“I’m just so proud of the effort that they have in each and every game,” said Lintal. “The way they show up to practice, they want to keep in their pads as long as they possibly can.”

Up next

After advancing out of the regional round, the State College Little Lions will take on the Williamsport Millionaires in the next round of the 6A PIAA playoffs.

title: Penn State CB pledge Deonte Flemings Jr.’s commitment is ‘strong’ after wrapping up junior season
author: Andrew Deal | Wrestling Editor
description:
4-star cornerback Deonte Flemings Jr. was the first player to make a pledge to the Nittany Lions under Matt Campbell, committing to Penn State on Jan. 31.

While he’s taken other visits during the 2026 season, Flemings still remains committed to Penn State, proving how strong the relationships he’s built with the coaching staff.

“My commitment is, I'm strong,” Flemings told The Daily Collegian. “I wouldn't have committed there if I didn't see myself going there. I built relationships over the years, and I feel great.”

Some of those relationships come from ones he’s had for multiple years, including Terry Smith, while others he’s built quicker, like with Campbell, who got him to commit to the Nittany Lions within two months of being the head coach.

Flemings said he’s “got great relationships” with the staff, and the coaches call him when they can to check in on the in-state product.

“Terry Smith, he built a relationship over the years with me,” Flemings said. “Right out of middle school, he started recruiting me my ninth grade year. Coach Campbell, he's a new guy from Iowa State, but great guy, really down to earth guy. I can't wait to be on campus and get to know those guys personally.”

The No. 5 player in Pennsylvania in the 2028 class understands the rich history the Penn State program has, something that Campbell has often mentioned since being with the Nittany Lions.

“Happy Valley is a place you want to be, definitely for school, development and also just you know building relationships,” Flemings said. “So it's a great school, a traditional school. It's a school you would want to be at.”

The McDowell product finished up his junior campaign with the Trojans after they fell to State College, 46-14, at Memorial Field, just two miles down the road from Beaver Stadium, his future home field.

“I wish we could have come out with the dub, but somebody gotta win, and the guys stay positive, and it felt great,” Flemings said. “(State College is) a great city, man. It's not that big, but it's just like where I'm from.”

Flemings saw himself grow the most through his leadership and “showing up for my team when they need me.”

On the field, he’s recognized key details as a cornerback that he’s developed as the season’s gone along, proving to be one of the top defensive backs in the nation.

“Being more patient at the line, and more patient in my backpedal, and actually reading the receivers movements,” Flemings said on details he’s improved on this season.

The Nittany Lion commit still has a little over 13 months until he’ll officially be enrolled at Penn State, where he’ll take that time to “get college ready.”
